correctness.rationale: For all fixed beta,eta>0, the exact finite hub/leaf-count generator yields O(m^(r/2)) stationary count moments in each fixed degree. The generator converges to the unique nonexplosive two-mode PDMP with drifts z-u and switching rates eta+beta^2*u and 1. The invariant law has no atoms because switch times have densities, is supported on [0,1] by contraction, and must have zero stationary flux by integrability at both endpoints. The two forward equations give the normalized densities f_0=u^(eta-1)(1-u) exp(beta^2*u)/Z and f_1=u^eta exp(beta^2*u)/Z. Uniform moment bounds and exchangeability yield all asserted covariances and the density-shape derivative test. Symbolic stationary-equation checks and exact finite-chain generators were executed from the actual accompanying verification script; no infinite claim rests on finite computations.

value.rationale: The square-root edge-transmission scale is imposed by the largest adjacency eigenvalue of a growing star, and permanently hub-targeted immigration is an interpretable localized intervention. At this scale a single fluctuating hub produces an order-square-root infected-leaf population with a fully explicit, non-Gaussian, nondegenerate stationary distribution; the conditional hub probability and two covariance amplitudes quantify persistent correlations not visible from mean-field prevalence alone. The boundary beta^2=1-eta, for 0<eta<1, is the exact density-shape crossover. These are structural observables of a natural epidemic process, not arbitrary numerical cases, and no survival-threshold result for the absorbing model is claimed.
